findings.title: Migration assumes the embed_category setting and matching category exist
findings.body: The migration calls execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i without checking whether the query returned a row. If the old embed_category site setting is absent, blank, or does not match a category name, result[0] is nil and the migration raises NoMethodError. The same assumption is made for uncategorized_category_id on line 15.

findings.title: Migration copies old embeddable hosts without normalizing them
findings.body: The migration inserts the old site-setting lines verbatim into embeddable_hosts.host. Old values could include schemes or paths, and the old code explicitly handled them. Direct SQL inserts bypass the model's before_validation normalization, while EmbeddableHost.record_for_host later matches only URI#host. Migrated rows like http://example.com or example.com/path will therefore never match incoming referers, breaking embedding after upgrade.

findings.title: Migration interpolates host values directly into SQL
findings.body: The INSERT statement embeds the host string h directly into the SQL string. If an old setting value contains a single quote or other SQL metacharacter, the migration can fail or execute unintended SQL. Use connection.quote or a parameterized insert.

findings.title: Destructive setting deletion is not reversible in a change migration
findings.body: The migration deletes the old embeddable_hosts and embed_category site settings inside a change method. Rails cannot automatically reverse this execute DELETE, so rolling back will not restore the previous configuration. Use up/down or make the data movement reversible if rollback support is expected.

findings.title: before_validation crashes when host is nil
findings.body: The before_validation callback unconditionally calls self.host.sub!. If a record is saved with a nil host, such as an API request that omits embeddable_host[host], this raises NoMethodError instead of producing a validation error. Guard against blank host and add a presence validation.

findings.title: Update and destroy do not handle missing records
findings.body: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update and #destroy fetch the record with EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and do not handle nil. For a nonexistent ID, update calls save_host(nil) and destroy calls nil.destroy, causing a 500 error. The actions should return a 404 when the host is not found.

findings.title: save_host assumes the embeddable_host params exist
findings.body: save_host accesses params[:embeddable_host][:host] and params[:embeddable_host][:category_id] without checking that params[:embeddable_host] is present. A request without that root key will raise NoMethodError. Use params.require or safe access with defaults.

findings.title: Host lookup does not downcase the parsed host
findings.body: record_for_host compares lower(host) in SQL to uri.host, but does not downcase uri.host before binding it. If a referer or URL contains an uppercase hostname, the comparison can fail because the literal is not lowercased. Use host.downcase or lower both sides in the query.

findings.title: Host lookup ignores ports even though validation allows ports
findings.body: The hostname validation regex allows a :port suffix, but record_for_host extracts only URI#host and queries the stored host column. A record saved as example.com:8080 will not match a request whose URI host is example.com, so hosts entered with ports will never be considered allowed. Port handling should be normalized consistently.

findings.title: No uniqueness validation or unique index on host
findings.body: EmbeddableHost does not validate host uniqueness and the table has no unique index. Duplicate host rows, including case variations, can be created. EmbeddableHost.record_for_host uses .first without an order, so category assignment becomes ambiguous if duplicates exist. Add a case-insensitive uniqueness validation and a unique index.

findings.title: Hostname regex rejects valid TLDs longer than five characters
findings.body: The host validation regex requires the TLD to be two to five letters. Valid domains with longer TLDs, such as .museum or newer gTLDs, cannot be saved as embeddable hosts.

findings.title: category_id is not validated
findings.body: save_host assigns category_id from request parameters and only replaces blank values with the uncategorized category ID. It does not verify that the category exists, so invalid or deleted category IDs can be persisted. This can leave embeddable hosts pointing at nonexistent categories and break category resolution in the client or importer.

findings.title: Plural embedded ID hydration assumes the value is an array
findings.body: The new plural hydration branch calls obj[k].map(...) for any key matching *_ids. If a serializer emits null or a non-array value for such a key, the store will throw TypeError. The code should verify the value is an array before mapping.

findings.title: record_for_host returns false instead of nil
findings.body: EmbeddableHost.record_for_host returns false when the input URL is invalid, but its name and usage imply it returns a record or nil. Returning false can cause surprising behavior for callers that expect a finder-style result. It should return nil in the failure cases.

findings.title: Controller specs only check inheritance
findings.body: The new admin controller specs only assert that the controllers subclass AdminController. They do not exercise create, update, destroy, missing records, missing params, invalid hosts, or category assignment. These are the paths where the migration/model/controller issues above occur.
